title: Add hysteresis-aware rollback oracle for perf canaries
author: Asha Khatri
description: Motivation: Our canary detectors occasionally trigger transient rollbacks during short-lived traffic perturbations or bursty tails. This PR introduces a Hysteresis-Aware Rollback Oracle (HARO) that reduces noisy rollback churn by reasoning over multi-timescale signals, trend direction, and a calibrated holdout retest policy. Design summary: HARO ingests detector alerts (latency, p90/p99, error-rate, throughput delta) and computes an ensemble score across three timescales (short=1m, medium=5m, long=30m). Instead of hard thresholds, HARO applies asymmetric hysteresis windows: stricter thresholds for opening a rollback (prevent regressions) and looser thresholds for closing one (avoid flip-flop). The oracle also schedules a non-disruptive retest probe against the candidate model with controlled traffic shadowing and compares retest metrics with the active model using a paired delta test. If the retest shows sustained degradation, HARO recommends rollback; otherwise it recommends pause and extended observation. Key features: 1) Multi-timescale signal fusion with time-decay weighted quantiles. 2) Asymmetric hysteresis (open/close thresholds configurable per-metric). 3) Retest probe scheduler with traffic quiesce and minimal live impact. 4) Confidence scoring to drive automated rollback, staged pause, or manual review. 5) Extensive observability hooks (explanation events, scoring breakdowns, and suggested remediation). Backwards compatibility: HARO is plumbed as an opt-in rollout guard; default behavior remains unchanged until enabled for a rollout policy. Implementation notes: New module perf/canary/haro.py contains the core oracle, with a lightweight C-extension stub for quantile maintenance perf (perf/canary/_quantile_accel.c). Integration in canary evaluator: perf/canary/evaluator.py adds an optional haro_client hook and new rollout decision path. Config: deploy/config/canary_oracles.yaml adds per-customer knobs (hysteresis_windows, retest_policy, probe_fraction). Tests: unit tests for ensemble fusion and hysteresis (perf/canary/tests/test_haro.py), integration test harness in perf-canary CI to simulate burst scenarios. Metrics emitted: haro.score, haro.timescale_contrib, haro.retest_result, haro.decision_reason. Security/ops: retest probes respect tenant isolation and do not send real customer data; all probe traffic is synthetic. Migration/rollout plan: 1) Canary-run HARO in passive mode for 1 week (score-only). 2) Enable active recommendations for internal rollouts (alpha). 3) Gate customer rollouts behind an opt-in feature flag. Related work: ENG-4123 (canary detector smoothing), ENG-5401 (probe scheduler), SRE-199 (rollback playbook). Checklist: - [x] Module implemented - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Docs update stubbed in repo - [x] Perf microbenchmarks run - [x] Observability events wired Known limitations: The retest probe currently uses a simple paired t-test; we may want to upgrade to a non-parametric test for heavy tails. Future work: incorporate upstream routing feedback (region-aware hysteresis) and automatic threshold calibration using historical baselines.

perf: add C quantile accel stub and Python bindings (perf/canary/_quantile_accel.c, setup)
test: add unit tests for hysteresis and retest logic (perf/canary/tests/test_haro.py)
ci: add integration scenario for transient-burst test (ci/perf-canary/scenarios/burst.yaml)
docs: add docs stub and configuration examples (docs/canary/haro.md)

release_notes:
- Adds Hysteresis-Aware Rollback Oracle (HARO) to reduce noisy rollback churn.
- Opt-in configuration for per-metric hysteresis and retest probes.
- Observability: haro.* metrics and explanation events.
review_conversation: Benji Morales: Nice direction. Can we ensure the retest probe fraction is configurable per-tenant? I'm worried about cost at scale.
Asha Khatri: Good call; added deploy/config/canary_oracles.yaml with per-tenant probe_fraction and default 0.1%
Priya Nair: The asymmetric hysteresis is clever. Please add a short justification in docs for the open/close ratios and include a recommended default.
Asha Khatri: Added rationale and defaults in docs/canary/haro.md; defaults chosen based on historical canary flakiness analysis (open:close = 1:3)
Ethan Liu: CI failed on the initial run due to missing build bindings for the C stub on the mac builder. Suggest a pure-Python fallback to avoid CI flakes.
Asha Khatri: Implemented fallback quantile accumulator in Python and updated setup to skip the C-extension on unsupported platforms; re-ran CI and green.
